> > So, if you want to set and forget a setting, I suggest you use setMklthreads(1)

messages.body_plain:
RRO has none of the scalability features that are part of RRE.

However, some functionality in R works really well, even with data sets as large as 100GB. These days it is not hard to create a machine (or virtual machine in the cloud) with large amounts of RAM.

However, your best course of action depends to a large extent on the exact nature of your analysis, and to some extent on the type and shape of your data.

You don't provide any details in your question, so I can't be much more specific.

As you point out, one of the fantastic advantages of RRE is that it makes it very easy to deal with very large data sets.

Regards

Andrie

messages.subject_clean: Problem installing MKL on Linux
messages.body_plain:
Hi Terry and Dwayne,

If the uninstall script doesn’t work, a workaround is to perform all of its steps by hand:

        rm $LIB_PATH/libmkl*

        rm $LIB_PATH/libiomp5.so

        rm $LIB_PATH/libRblas.so

        rm $LIB_PATH/libRlapack.so

        mv $LIB_PATH/libRblas.so.keep $LIB_PATH/libRblas.so

        mv $LIB_PATH/libRlapack.so.keep $LIB_PATH/libRlapack.so

        ## remove env variables from Rprofile.site

        sed -i -e '/MKL_INTERFACE_LAYER/d' $ETC_PATH/Rprofile.site

        sed -i -e '/MKL_THREADING_LAYER/d' $ETC_PATH/Rprofile.site

        echo "remove.packages('RevoUtilsMath')" | $R_PATH -q --no-save > mkl_log.txt 2>&1

($LIB_PATH is typically /usr/lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib/R/lib—it’s the path to R shared libraries.)

Please let us know how that goes.

Also please let us know if you've upgraded from a previous version of RRO.

Thanks,

Josée

Hi David,

Apologies for asking a rather simple question which I'm sure you've been asked many times!

If one uses Revo R Open for commercial use is it acceptable to use Intel MKL BLAS/LAPACK as provided by your website?

You mentioned: "We're pleased that we're able to partner with Intel to offer it to all RRO users free of charge". However this could mean that the optional add-on of Intel MKL provided by your firm is only available to people who have an Intel MKL commercial license.

Your help would be appreciated. Basically if someone doesn't have the Intel MKL commercial license can they still download the MKL libraries your website and use them commercially? I think not however I'm not sure.

Regards,

Hamaad.

David Smith
